_doc: Processing recipes of the assistant. {x} is the input data, {t} the time in seconds from the first sample, {dt} the median sample period in seconds. They hold in absolute time (ns) and in pulse time (s), and the windows stay in seconds when a zoom fetches the data with another decimation. "describe" goes to the Comment column; "title" and "plain" are what the card shows, in everyday words.

savgol.label: Savitzky-Golay

seconds.ask: Sure. Over how long should I smooth it, for example 10 s?

savgol.expr: scipy.signal.savgol_filter({x}, window_length=2 * np.int64(np.maximum(2, np.round({seconds} / {dt} / 2))) + 1, polyorder=2, mode='nearest')
savgol.title: Smoothing
savgol.plain: smoothed over {duration}, keeping the peaks sharp

median.label: Median filter

seconds.ask: Sure. Over how long should I look for spikes, for example 10 s?

median.title: Spike removal
median.plain: spikes removed, comparing each point with the {duration} around it

lowpass.label: Low-pass filter

hz.ask: Sure. Which frequency should I keep up to, for example 1 Hz for changes slower than about once a second?

lowpass.describe: low-pass filter at {hz} Hz (Butterworth, order 4, no phase shift)
lowpass.title: Noise filter
lowpass.plain: fast noise removed, keeping changes slower than {hz} Hz

derivative.label: Derivative
derivative.title: Rate of change
derivative.plain: how fast it changes, per second

log10.label: Log10
log10.describe: base-10 logarithm of the values, leaving out zero and below (for a log axis, ask for log scale instead)
log10.title: Logarithm
log10.plain: base-10 logarithm of the values; zero and below are left out
